questions.question: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: EXPORT OF SAMBALPURI SAREES
questions.answer: The Ministry outlined NHDP and RMSS interventions, export-promotion support, and GI registration status for Sambalpuri Bandha Saree & Fabrics.
questions.answerFull:
Ministry of Textiles through Office of Development Commissioner (Handlooms) promotes handloom products including Bargarh under National Handloom Development Programme and Raw Material Supply Scheme.

Under these schemes, assistance is provided for raw material, upgraded looms and accessories, worksheds, skilling, design development, technical/common infrastructure, domestic and international marketing, concessional loans under weavers' MUDRA scheme, and social security.

Support for international marketing linkages and participation in fairs/exhibitions, buyer-seller meets and branding initiatives (India Handloom Brand and Handloom Mark) is also provided.

Raw Material Supply Scheme provides reimbursed freight and 15% subsidy for eligible yarn categories.

Sambalpuri Bandha Saree & Fabrics is registered under the GI Act, 1999.

This information was provided by THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR TEXTILES SHRI PABITRA MARGHERITA in a written reply to a question in Lok Sabha today.

questions.question: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: PROMOTION OF TRADITIONAL HANDLOOM PRODUCTS
questions.answer: The Ministry listed schemes, GI support, design centres, marketing expos, producer companies, and GeM onboarding for weavers/artisans.
questions.answerFull:
To promote handloom and handicraft sectors, Ministry of Textiles is implementing National Handloom Development Programme, Raw Material Supply Scheme, National Handicrafts Development Programme, and Comprehensive Handicrafts Cluster Development Scheme.

Under these schemes, assistance is provided for raw materials, common infrastructure, marketing in domestic/overseas markets, and Weaver MUDRA loans.

Additional measures include GI registration support, design resource centres, marketing expos/events, formation of producer companies, and onboarding weavers/artisans on GeM.

Funds are not allocated state-wise and are released based on proposals from states and organizations.

This information was provided by THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR TEXTILES SHRI PABITRA MARGHERITA in a written reply to a question in Lok Sabha today.

questions.question: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: IMPOSITION OF DIGITAL TOOLS
questions.answer: The Ministry stated no guidelines were issued on use of tools like Slack by government employees and cited broader cyberspace policy focus.
questions.answerFull:
The policies of the Government of India are aimed at ensuring a safe, trusted and accountable cyberspace for users in the country.

Key regulatory initiatives by Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology focus on strengthening legal frameworks, enhancing data protection and cybersecurity infrastructure, and awareness.

Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions has not issued any guidelines related to use of digital tools like Slack by Government employees.

This information was given by Dr. Jitendra Singh, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, in a written reply in the Lok Sabha today.
questions.ministry: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions

questions.question: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: DEVELOPMENT OF SILK SECTOR
questions.answer: Government shared Silk Samagra-2 outlay, assistance released, beneficiary coverage, and support provided to Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.
questions.answerFull:
The Government through Central Silk Board has been implementing Silk Samagra-2 with an outlay of Rs. 4,679.85 crore for 2021-22 to 2025-26 for development of sericulture.

Assistance is provided to states for beneficiary-oriented interventions across pre-cocoon and post-cocoon components.

So far, central assistance of Rs. 1,075.58 crore has been provided to cover around 78,000 beneficiaries under Silk Samagra-2.

Based on proposals, central assistance of Rs. 72.50 crore to Andhra Pradesh and Rs. 40.66 crore to Telangana has been provided during the last three years including the current year.

The Government is also implementing RMSS and NHDP to promote the handloom sector.

This information was provided by THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR TEXTILES SHRI PABITRA MARGHERITA in a written reply to a question in Rajya Sabha today.
